declaration.goal: Move the body as far as possible in the direction it faces at the start: maximise x.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN one channel is held at +1 for the whole trial and the other four are 0, THE system SHALL move the body by a distance that depends on the channel, and with all channels at 0 THE system SHALL stay near the start.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Baseline (all 0) x=2.5e-5 m, inside P1. c0 at +1 gave x=1.8e-5 m, inside P2 but trivially (no motion). Constant levels never translate the body: |x|<0.03 m, |y|<0.02 m for all channels. Constant c2, c3, c4 give a small heading step (+1.7, -3.9, -1.66 deg) that settles within ~0.1 s, so those channels act on posture or heading, not on translation. c0 and c1 at +1 give heading ~0 (-0.001, -0.004), like baseline. The hypothesis that a constant channel moves the body by a channel-dependent distance is not supported. Picture shows a small body in a 5x2 grid of frames, no visible displacement.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN channel c1 alone carries a 1 Hz sine of amplitude 1, THE system SHALL move the body forward by more than 0.05 m, and WHEN all five channels carry the same in-phase sine THE system SHALL stay within 0.02 m of the start.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: c1 alone at 1 Hz gave x=2.5e-5, identical to baseline, so c1 has no effect alone. P2 missed narrowly: all channels in phase gave x=-0.0249 m, heading 116.7 deg, y=0.12 m. Single channels at 1 Hz (x, y, heading): c0 (3.9e-5, 2e-6, 0.004), c1 (2.5e-5, -5e-6, -0.004), c2 (0.027, 0.024, 22.9 deg), c3 (-0.028, -0.016, -1.2 deg), c4 (0.002, 0.010, 5.8 deg). c0 and c1 do nothing alone; c2 turns the body, c3 and c4 wiggle it. All in phase gives heading 116.7 deg, much more than the sum of the parts (23-1.2+5.8), so channels interact; c0 or c1 may gate or amplify c2..c4. Translation stays at the centimetre level in every trial.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0 is held at +1 and c2 carries a 1 Hz sine, THE system SHALL turn by more than 40 deg, and WHEN c1 is held at +1 instead THE system SHALL turn by less than 40 deg.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: with c0 held at +1 and a 1 Hz sine on c2, heading was 24.5 deg, inside E2's single-channel value (22.9 deg), not above 40. P2 hit (c1 held: 22.7 deg, inside [-40,40]) but only because c1 has no effect. Every trial matches the E2 single-channel trial of the same sine channel to within ~2 deg and 2 mm (c3: x=-0.0324/-0.0282, c4: heading 7.4/5.8). A constant on c0 or c1 has no gating or amplifying effect. The in-phase result of E2 (heading 117 deg) must come from the sine on c0/c1 or from interaction among c2, c3, c4 sines.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2, c3 and c4 carry the same in-phase 1 Hz sine and c0, c1 are 0, THE system SHALL turn by more than 60 deg, and WHEN only c0 and c1 carry the sine THE system SHALL stay within 5 deg of the start heading.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P2 hit: c0+c1 sine gave heading 0.004 deg, identical to baseline, so c0 and c1 are inert here (also with c2 added, 25.8 vs 22.9 deg for c2 alone). P1 hit (126.4 deg for c2+c3+c4, above 60). Pairs: c2+c3 73.5 deg, c2+c4 56.9, c3+c4 67.6. The turn is not the sum of single-channel turns (c3 alone -1.2 deg, c4 alone 5.8 deg but c3+c4 gives 67.6), so c2, c3 and c4 interact and in-phase drive of two of them turns the body. Translation stays tiny: |x| < 0.05 m, y up to 0.13 m, all consistent with arc motion plus wobble. In-phase drive never produces useful forward motion; phase offset between channels is the next thing to try.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 carries sin(2 pi t) and c3 carries the same sine delayed by 180 deg, THE system SHALL turn by less than 30 deg in magnitude, and WHEN the delay is 90 deg THE system SHALL move forward by more than 0.05 m.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 hit: phi=180 gave heading -7.6 deg (in [-30,30]), x=0.023 m. P2 hit but only just: phi=90 gave x=0.0514 m (limit 0.05). Full phi sweep (x m, heading deg): 45: 0.068, 82.6; 90: 0.051, 56.5; 135: -0.004, 23.3; 180: 0.023, -7.6; 225: 0.061, -23.9; 270: 0.042, -4.2. Heading falls monotonically from +83 at phi=45 to -24 at phi=225, so phase offset sets turn direction and rate. x is largest near phi=45 and 225 (6-7 cm) and smallest near 135, so x has two humps per cycle of phi. Translation is still only a few cm at 1 Hz; next try frequency.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 and c3 carry sines with c3 lagging c2 by 270 deg and the frequency rises from 1 Hz to 2 Hz or 4 Hz, THE system SHALL travel farther in x, with x over 0.08 m at 2 Hz and over 0.15 m at 4 Hz.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 hit: f=2 Hz gave x=0.144 m (>0.08). P2 missed: f=4 Hz gave x=0.117 m (<0.15). Sweep with phi=270 (f: x, y, heading): 0.5: 0.055, 0.052, 11; 2: 0.144, 0.161, -6; 3: 0.036, 0.143, 9.9; 4: 0.117, 0.139, 20; 6: 0.079, 0.144, 44; 8: 0.012, 0.062, 32. x does not grow monotonically with f. Best is 2 Hz; 3 Hz is low. y is positive and about as large as x at f>=2, so the body drifts left as well as forward. Final x also contains a wobble of a few cm from the tracked point, so single-point x is noisy by about 0.02 m.

statement.author: dr-kiro

words.text: All three predictions hit. f=1.5, phi=270: x=0.048 (in [0.03,0.14]); f=2.5, phi=270: x=0.085 (in [0.03,0.14]); f=2, phi=225: x=0.241 m (in [0.1,0.4]), the best so far, with heading -16.6 deg and y=0.083. x peaks near 2 Hz (parabola fit through 1.5/2/2.5 Hz gives a peak near 2.06 Hz) and phi=225 beats phi=270 at 2 Hz (0.241 vs 0.144), as at 1 Hz (0.061 vs 0.042). 1.5 Hz and 2.5 Hz traces show y drifting left (0.17, 0.19 m) with heading +26 and +16 deg, while 225 deg lag turns the body slightly right.
